title: E5: reasoning-budget recovery and test controller on harder tasks (preregistered)

H_RM.comparison: turn after an exhausted turn is non-empty: recovery arms vs baseline arms

hypothesis: Handing a model the tail of reasoning that ran out of budget, with thinking off for one turn, turns empty replies into actions and raises success on tasks a 4B model finds hard.
finding: Preregistered verdicts. Primary: H_R recover vs none inconclusive (4 wins, 0 losses, p=0.0625: the margin rule wins-losses>=4 is met, p<0.05 is not); H_RM mechanism supported (the turn after an exhausted turn was non-empty in 39/39 recovery-arm followups vs 23/39 baseline, one-sided Fisher p=2.2e-6). Secondary: H_C controller vs none supported (9 wins, 0 losses, p=0.002); H_CR controller_recover vs controller inconclusive (3-1, p=0.31). Success: none 3/18, recover 7/18, controller 12/18, controller_recover 14/18. The recovery does what it was built to do; whether it raises success was not shown at this sample size. The test-driven controller, not supported on E2's near-ceiling tasks, is supported on tasks Qwen fails unaided.

exploratory.note: Not preregistered. Written after the verdicts above.
exploratory.mechanism_is_partly_by_construction: The recovery turn runs with thinking off, so it cannot spend its budget thinking; a non-empty reply is close to guaranteed. H_RM confirms the intervention fires and is honoured by the server, not that it helps. Per run: recovery arms had exhaustion in 13 runs and 0 ended on three empty replies; baseline arms had exhaustion in 16 runs and 6 ended that way (all 6 'empty replies' errors in the experiment).
exploratory.fewer_exhausted_turns: recover had 6 exhausted turns vs 17 in none (controller_recover 34 vs controller 32). Without a controller, exhaustion clustered: baseline exhausted turns often followed one another.
exploratory.where_recover_won: The 4 H_R wins are on e5d (2), e5e (1) and e5f (1). e5g was solved by every arm in every seed (ceiling); excluding it, none 0/15, recover 4/15, controller 9/15, controller_recover 11/15.
exploratory.speed: Median wall time: none 97 s, recover 50 s, controller 87 s, controller_recover 64 s. Median completion tokens per run: none 9179, recover 3855.
exploratory.runs_that_exhausted_still_fail: Among runs with at least one exhausted turn, success was none 0/7, recover 1/5, controller 4/9, controller_recover 4/8. Recovery keeps the run alive; it does not by itself make the model right.
exploratory.malformed_tool_call: One recover run (e5f, seed 44) ended on HTTP 500: llama.cpp rejected the model's tool-call arguments as invalid JSON. Model behaviour, counted as a failure as the judge prescribes.

limits: Six tasks by the same author as the arms, 18 paired units, one 4B model, one engine (llama.cpp b11146 CUDA on Slink; not pooled with the Mac or with E2). Seeds vary sampling only and CUDA sampling is not bit-exact; E5 has no identical-treatment pair to measure that noise. The recovery bundles two changes (reasoning tail carried over, thinking off for one turn) and does not separate them. One controller_recover run overran the 1200 s limit by waiting 1800 s on an unattended approval (see the amendment); it ties in H_CR whatever its outcome would have been.
